courthouses.name: Tani G. Cantil-Sakauye Sacramento County Courthouse
courthouses.hours: Building: Mon–Fri 7:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m. Criminal clerk: Mon–Fri 8:30 a.m.–4:00 p.m. ((916) 874-5522 option 1). Civil Self-Help (2nd floor, Room 250): Mon/Tue/Wed/Fri 8:30–12:00 and 1:30–4:00; Thu 8:30–12:00.
courthouses.note: Main criminal courthouse: felony and misdemeanor trials, criminal pretrial matters, DUI cases and arraignments, plus felony/misdemeanor filing, fees and case processing. 53 courtrooms on floors 3–17; courtroom names give floor + position (e.g. 3A = west side of 3rd floor). Replaced the Gordon D. Schaber courthouse at 720 9th St (no longer on the court's location list). Phone option 1 = Criminal, 3 = Civil, 4 = Jury.
courthouses.todo: Per-department criminal assignments not published on the location page; departments left empty.

courthouses.name: Lorenzo Patiño Hall of Justice
courthouses.hours: Mon–Fri (except court holidays) 8:30 a.m.–12:30 p.m. and 1:30–4:00 p.m.
courthouses.note: Same building as the Sacramento County Main Jail. Houses the Criminal Division's felony and misdemeanor pretrial 'Home Court' departments, two of which also serve as the Domestic Violence Court and Drug Court. Departments 60–63 (first floor).

departments.label: Department 60
departments.note: Court lists Depts 60–63 here; which two are DV Court and Drug Court not stated

courthouses.todo: No phone published for this location; use (916) 874-5522 option 1 (Criminal) — not confirmed as covering this building.

courthouses.name: Carol Miller Justice Center
courthouses.hours: Mon–Thu 7:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m.; closed Fridays and court holidays. Traffic call center: Mon–Fri 4 a.m.–9 p.m., Sat–Sun 6 a.m.–3 p.m. Night Court 2nd Wednesday of each month 5:15–6:15 p.m.
courthouses.note: Traffic misdemeanors and infractions (arraignment, pretrial hearings, trials — adults), juvenile traffic infractions, small claims and unlawful detainer. Departments 81–84 (1st floor) and 86–88 (3rd floor). Phone shown is the Traffic Division Call Center; Small Claims/UD: (916) 875-7746.

courthouses.name: Juvenile Courthouse
courthouses.hours: Building Mon–Fri 8:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m.; business hours Mon–Fri 8:10 a.m.–12:00 p.m. and 1:00–4:00 p.m.
courthouses.note: Juvenile Dependency and Juvenile Justice (delinquency) — Departments 90–97. Not an adult criminal court.

courthouses.name: William R. Ridgeway Family Relations Courthouse
courthouses.note: Family law courthouse; not a criminal court.
courthouses.todo: Hours not loaded from the facility detail page.

public_defenders.name: Sacramento County Public Defender — Main Office (Felony, Major Crimes & Misdemeanor Divisions)
public_defenders.note: Office is on the ground floor; enter on the first floor and take stairs/elevator down.

public_defenders.name: Sacramento County Public Defender — Juvenile Division

legal_aid.name: Sacramento County Public Defender — Expungement assistance
legal_aid.serves: Adults with Sacramento County convictions who have completed probation (or were discharged early) and are not serving a sentence or on probation for another offense
legal_aid.what: Help with PC 1203.4 expungement petitions; walk-in Tuesdays 2:00–4:00 p.m. at 700 H Street, Suite 0270, first-come first-served. Requires mitigation documents (including a personal statement) before a petition is filed.
legal_aid.todo: Details confirmed via search snippet of the official PD page; direct fetch returned 404 (site migrated). Re-verify hours/phone on the new PD site.

legal_aid.name: Sacramento Superior Court — Civil Self-Help Services
legal_aid.what: Court self-help center; expungement of criminal convictions is among its listed topics. The court's Expungement self-help page explains PC 1203.4 dismissal.
legal_aid.note: Location (500 G St., 2nd floor, Room 250) and hours from the court's courthouse page; phone/email from the Sacramento County Public Law Library expungement page (saclaw.org).

legal_aid.name: Legal Services of Northern California — Sacramento Office
legal_aid.what: Free civil legal aid (housing, public benefits incl. CalWorks, CalFresh, Medi-Cal, GA, SSI, unemployment, SDI). Does not list criminal or record-clearance work.
legal_aid.note: 515 12th Street, Sacramento 95814. Intake Mon/Tue/Thu/Fri 8:30–12 and 1–5; after-hours intake line (866) 815-5990.

probation.name: Sacramento County Probation — Adult Office (reporting / find your officer)
probation.note: Call (916) 875-0300 for reporting instructions. To find your probation officer, call (916) 874-PROB (7762) with your X-reference number (touch-tone).

probation.name: Sacramento County Probation — Adult Court Services (incl. Pretrial)
probation.todo: Hours not listed on the page.

programs.name: Probation Pretrial Unit (pretrial monitoring)
programs.summary: Created in 2019. Probation assesses people booked into custody and monitors people the Superior Court releases to Pretrial, at no cost to them. Monitoring may include court reminder calls, office visits, community visits and GPS monitoring.

programs.name: Adult Recovery Court
programs.summary: Residential and outpatient treatment for people charged with non-violent drug possession, drug-related probation violations and certain other drug-related and property crimes; monitored and tested by Probation.

programs.name: Mental Health Treatment Court (MHTC)
programs.summary: Post-plea program for defendants with qualifying mental health or co-occurring disorders; DA reviews referrals and approves acceptance. Individualized treatment plan with close court monitoring.

programs.name: Mental Health Diversion (PC 1001.36)
programs.summary: For people charged with a misdemeanor or felony whose treatable mental disorder played a significant part in the charged offense.

programs.name: Drug Diversion (PC 1000)
programs.summary: For first-time simple drug possession: 40 hours of drug education, monthly meetings, support groups, 6 months of drug testing; monitored by Probation.

programs.name: Military Diversion Program (PC 1001.80)
programs.summary: For current/former U.S. military members charged with misdemeanors or felonies who may suffer from service-related trauma, TBI, PTSD, substance abuse or mental health problems.

programs.name: DUI Treatment Court (DUITC)
programs.summary: For people charged with DUI who have three prior DUI misdemeanor convictions within 10 years; mandatory in-custody period, Probation supervision and treatment.

programs.name: ReSET Court (Reducing Sexual Exploitation and Trafficking)
programs.summary: For people charged with prostitution or prostitution-related offenses; initial referral to Community Against Sexual Harm (CASH).

programs.name: Domestic Violence Court
programs.summary: Dedicated courtroom; people charged with DV or related offenses are automatically set for pretrial hearings here. Also handles Batterer's Treatment compliance.

programs.name: Loaves and Fishes Court
programs.summary: For unhoused defendants with low-level traffic and some misdemeanor offenses who cannot pay fines/fees; community service at Loaves and Fishes works off fines (does not dismiss the case).

programs.name: HEAP Expungement Calendar
programs.summary: Expedited expungement calendar for unhoused people who completed probation, with the Public Defender and DA; contact the Public Defender.

jails.name: Sacramento County Main Jail
jails.phone_note: Main Jail line (also inmate info and SIRENS release-notification registration). Public hours 7:00 a.m.–11:00 p.m. daily. Non-emergency (916) 874-5115. Family emergencies: Main Jail Social Worker (916) 874-6345.
jails.court_ids_note: The Lorenzo Patiño Hall of Justice courtrooms (Depts 60–63) are in the same building as the Main Jail; Cantil-Sakauye is the main criminal courthouse two blocks away. Nearest, not confirmed as the transport destination.
jails.todo: Sheriff's page does not say whether the Main Jail houses men, women or both. Money: TouchPay kiosk in lobby, (866) 232-1899, gtlfsonlinepay.com; facility number 257501.

jails.name: Rio Cosumnes Correctional Center (RCCC)
jails.phone_note: RCCC public line. Primary custody facility for people sentenced to county jail; also holds pre-sentence detainees, federal and reciprocal prisoners, and parole violators. Inmate phones: Securus 1-800-844-6591.
jails.court_ids_note: Nearest criminal courthouses, not confirmed. The RCCC page does not name a court destination.
jails.note: Visiting schedule lists male general population, male protective custody and female population units (houses: both).

bail.note: Before paying a bail agent, check their license with the California Department of Insurance license lookup. The court's Felony and Misdemeanor Bail Schedule is linked from saccourt.ca.gov/divisions/criminal (https://www.saccourt.ca.gov/home/showpublisheddocument/407/639123699099530000). For custody status call the Main Jail at (916) 874-6752. This is information only, not legal advice.
